analysis:
At the Delhi End TB Summit on 13 March 2018, the Prime Minister announced a target of TB elimination in India by 2025, five years ahead of the global SDG deadline of 2030.

The WHO Global TB Report 2024 recorded that TB returned as the world's leading infectious disease killer in 2023, and that India carried the largest share of the global burden. Press analyses of the WHO Global TB Report 2025 state that India recorded roughly 27.1 lakh cases and more than 3 lakh deaths in 2024. A March 2026 Newslaundry analysis based on 2025 case numbers put India's incidence at about 185 per 100,000 population, more than four times the National Strategic Plan's 2025 elimination threshold. India's incidence decline between 2015 and 2024 was faster than the global average, but the absolute elimination target for 2025 was not met.

Government releases describe the campaign as ongoing under the National TB Elimination Programme and cite improvements in case detection and treatment.
notes: The speech was delivered in Hindi; quote_english is the PMO/PIB English rendering and quote_original is the PMO India tweet excerpt carried on narendramodi.in. 'Elimination' is conventionally defined as under 1 case per million population per year, far below observed incidence. WHO notes that burden estimates are revised annually and comparisons across report editions are not appropriate. The Hindu (article68845844) and The Wire also reported that the 2025 target would be missed; those URLs were seen in search results but the exact publication dates were not confirmed, so they are not listed as evidence.
